correctness.rationale: For every q=p^e, n=q-1 is prime to p. Pullback under [X^n:Y^n:Z^n] is etale on the torus. The exact conic matrix/differential and axis restrictions exhaust possible singular parameters. At lambda=0 Cremona gives the irreducible Fermat normalization and ordinary n-fold vertices. At -1/3 an explicit product of two degree-n Fermat forms gives n^2 transverse nodes. At -1/4 the Heron identity gives four degree-(n/2) smooth components with six pairwise intersection sets of n/2 points each and contact order n/2; no triple intersections. Infinity is double Fermat. Exact symbolic identities and several complete finite-field point enumerations were independently rerun from the packaged verifier, but the infinite-family conclusion rests on the proof.

value.rationale: This is the exhaustive geometric discriminant/fiber classification of a natural fixed pencil introduced for large automorphism groups. It distinguishes two- and four-component Fermat degenerations, a Cremona-transformed irreducible singular member, and their characteristic-dependent local ADE/contact types. The four-component fiber has 3(q-1) high-contact A_{q-2} points, not merely isolated factorization trivia; the classification can be used in studying degenerations and normalizations of these invariant curves. The known description of the pencil alone does not supply these boundary invariants.
